title: Ganguly and Rahane Join Prince William for Tennis-Ball Cricket on The Mall
excerpt: The former India captains played alongside Brian Lara, Joe Root and Harry Brook outside Buckingham Palace in a Royal Foundation event counting down to the Earthshot Prize in Mumbai on November 17.
body:
• Sourav Ganguly and Ajinkya Rahane played tennis-ball cricket with Prince William on The Mall, outside Buckingham Palace, on October 13.
  • Brian Lara, Joe Root and Harry Brook also took part in the friendly match, held under a Royal Foundation release.
  • The event marked the countdown to the Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai on November 17, 2026 — the prize's first edition in India.
  • Rahane called playing on The Mall, with Buckingham Palace behind him, an experience that will stay with him for a long time.

Former India captains Sourav Ganguly and Ajinkya Rahane joined Prince William for a friendly game of tennis-ball cricket on The Mall in London, the ceremonial avenue outside Buckingham Palace, according to a press release from The Royal Foundation reported by ANI via New Kerala.

The match was not a competitive fixture. It was staged to celebrate the shared place of cricket in India and the United Kingdom and to build momentum for an environmental cause: the Earthshot Prize, which Prince William launched in 2020 through The Royal Foundation.

Who Was on The Mall

Alongside Ganguly and Rahane, the gathering included West Indies great Brian Lara and England players Joe Root and Harry Brook, Hindusthan Samachar reported. Rahane, who was invited by Prince William, has recently called time on his own playing career, making the outing one of his first public cricket appearances since stepping away from the professional game.

The setting did much of the work. The Mall is normally reserved for royal occasions and grand processions; for one morning it served as an improvised pitch, with Buckingham Palace as the backdrop.

"Cricket has taken me to some incredible grounds around the world, but playing tennis-ball cricket on The Mall in London, with Buckingham Palace in the background, is an experience that will stay with me for a long time."

— Ajinkya Rahane

Why the Match Was Held

Rahane, writing on LinkedIn on Wednesday, said the day celebrated the shared love of cricket between India and the UK but was mainly about a cause beyond sport. The players discussed cricket's unifying power, their memories of playing in England and India, and a shared responsibility toward the future — of the game and of the planet.

He linked that responsibility to the values cricket teaches: discipline, teamwork and honest effort, applied to protecting nature, clean air and oceans, cutting waste and tackling climate change.

The Earthshot Prize, founded in 2020, backs practical solutions to environmental problems and has become the Royal Foundation's flagship programme. Taking its ceremony to India for the first time, with Mumbai as host, gives the London cricket gathering a direct line to next month's event.

The Mumbai Connection

The London match was a countdown event. The sixth edition of the Earthshot Prize will be held in Mumbai on November 17, 2026, marking the award's debut in India. Rahane, a Mumbai native, said he was looking forward to welcoming the event to his home city.

For Indian cricket, the optics are straightforward: two former captains, one of them the game's most recognisable Indian ambassador of his generation in Ganguly, fronting an India-linked global event on one of London's most famous streets — a reminder that cricket remains the most natural bridge between the two countries.
